title: Associations Between Emotional Competence and Emotional Empathy in Secondary-Level Vocational Nursing Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
content: Empathy is essential to humanized nursing care, yet its relationship with emotional competence before professional entry remains insufficiently specified. This cross-sectional study examined whether distinct dimensions of emotional competence were differentially associated with emotional empathy among secondary-level vocational nursing students in Croatia. A total of 337 students enrolled in a five-year program for general care nurses/medical technicians completed the Emotional Skills and Competence Questionnaire (ESCQ-45) and the Emotional Empathy Scale from the E-Questionnaire. Spearman correlations and hierarchical linear regression were applied, with adjustment for sex and clinical exposure at the time of assessment. Emotional empathy correlated positively with emotion perception and understanding (ρ = 0.346, p &lt; 0.001) and emotion management (ρ = 0.281, p &lt; 0.001), but not with emotion expression and naming (ρ = 0.099, p = 0.070). In the adjusted model, emotion perception and understanding (β = 0.254, p &lt; 0.001), emotion management (β = 0.254, p &lt; 0.001), and sex (β = 0.277, p &lt; 0.001) remained significant predictors, whereas clinical exposure was not significant. Emotion expression and naming showed a negative partial association only after adjustment. The findings support a dimensional interpretation of emotional competence and suggest that emotional empathy in this educational context is more closely related to recognising, understanding, and regulating emotions than to expressive emotional skills considered in isolation.
